spec.engine_series: wide monthly return minus ladder monthly return
spec.ladder: k = 0..n carries removed in |delta contribution| order, each removed from BOTH arms' era levels
spec.ladder_base: anchored on the PUBLISHED era levels, because the decomposition's own levels carry a compounding offset that can exceed the delta
spec.verdict: agree when the two eroded engine levels share a sign, disagree otherwise, undefined when either level is exactly zero
spec.delta_span: share_of_delta_removed_pct is cumulative |dropped contribution| over |delta|; beyond 100% the rung has removed more than the delta is made of and is flagged beyond_delta_span

corrections.issue: E174 read both of its drop points off the decomposition's own era levels, whose offset from the published levels is up to 55.8bp -- larger than the delta being attributed. Its 'gone at top1, back at top5' pair is therefore a property of that base, not of the carriers.
corrections.corrected_reading: anchored on the published levels, 2024_now's disagreement survives every rung inside its own delta span and only breaks once more than the delta has been removed; the published TILT3SIGNNAMES face is frozen as-is and this face is the reading to quote
corrections.discovered_by: this leg's k=0 verdict disagreeing with the headline on the first cut

honest: 2024_now: read off its own decomposition the era would print 'agree' instead of 'disagree', so the carrier ladder is only meaningful anchored (offset -52.9bp raw / -55.8bp screened)
the ladder is anchored on the published era levels and every rung removes one carrier's contribution from both arms, so k=0 IS the headline and every later rung is auditable arithmetic

the unanchored decomposition base is published beside it because the gap between the two bases is larger than the delta on some eras; where that gap alone flips a sign, a verdict read off the unanchored base says nothing about the carriers
a returning verdict is not a defect: it says the two arms' signs were separated by a small set of name-months, which is exactly what a two-point sample could not show
the ladder is published with its delta coverage because past 100% it is eroding more than the delta, and a verdict read there is about the eroded books, not about the repair
eras whose engine level did not move are the built-in control: a ladder that is not flat there is broken before it reads anything
